transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... things have just been a bit much lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been holding it together at work alright, but at home and with my coursework, I’m just... I'm a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. 

I've also noticed I’ve started skipping the things that usually keep my head clear. I haven't been going fishing, or doing my woodworking, or even attending the first-aid workshops I usually like. I just figured I should probably talk to someone to get a handle on it.

When you feel 'wound up,' are you mostly worried about specific stressors related to your father-in-law moving in, or do you find yourself feeling anxious and worried about a wide range of different things in your daily life?

It's really just about him moving in. I don't think I'm worrying about a whole bunch of different things. It's more just... the disruption at home, having an extra person in our space. I'm not feeling anxious about my job or, you know, random everyday stuff. It all pretty much comes back to the new situation at the house.
Beyond feeling wound up and short-tempered, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or really down. Like I mentioned, I have stopped doing some of my hobbies, like the woodworking and fishing, but it's not because I've lost interest in them. It's more that I just... I don't feel like I have the time or the mental space for them right now with everything going on at the house. I still like those things, I'm just not doing them. So, no, no real feelings of being depressed or anything like that. Just stressed.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since your father-in-law moved in?

No, not really. My sleep has been... about the same as always. I still sleep pretty well, even with the extra tension around the house. And my appetite hasn't changed either. I'm still eating normally. So, yeah, no real issues with either of those.
Have you found yourself feeling particularly tearful or sad since your father-in-law moved in?

No, I haven't. I'm not really a tearful guy anyway, but... no, I haven't felt sad about it. It's really just the frustration of having my routine upended and dealing with the extra tension. So, no crying or feeling down, just that same irritation I was talking about.
